scope: stable finite non-negative rational recurrent total-mass systems, explicit positive rational branch/gauge coordinates, and finite declared positive feedback-event sets

theorems.statement: Z_loop(W)=1/det(I-W)=det((I-W)^(-1)) and Gamma(W)=-ln det(I-W)=sum_{k>=1} tr(W^k)/k. Gamma is invariant under positive diagonal state gauge, additive across SCC diagonal blocks, insensitive to feed-forward inter-SCC weights, and Gamma=0 iff the positive-support digraph is acyclic.

theorems.hypotheses: same as T17; write W=A/D and B=DI-A with A integer non-negative
theorems.statement: With delta=det(B)>0 and C=adj(B), h0=C*1 is a positive integer vector satisfying B h0=delta*1, equivalently A h0=D h0-delta*1. Moreover Z_loop=D^n/delta and the canonical potential x=(I-W)^(-1)1 equals (D/delta) h0.
theorems.consequence: The same exact integer determinant is the uniform canonical potential slack and the recurrent zeta denominator after common-denominator clearing.

theorems.hypotheses: stable finite positive rational system; explicit branch e:a->b with weight q_e>0; S=(I-W)^(-1)
theorems.statement: R_e=dGamma/d ln(q_e)=q_e S_ba. R_e>0 iff e lies on a directed recurrent cycle and R_e=0 for transient/feed-forward edges. Sum_e R_e=tr(S-I).
theorems.integer_form: After common-denominator clearing W=A/D, S=(D/delta) adj(DI-A), so every response is exact rational with integer numerator/denominator certificate.

theorems.hypotheses: same stable explicit-branch scope as T19; e:a->b, f:c->d
theorems.statement: In log branch-weight coordinates, H_ef=delta_ef R_e + q_e q_f S_bc S_da. H is exact rational, symmetric and positive semidefinite. On a strongly connected recurrent support its kernel is exactly the vertex-gauge coboundary space, hence rank(H)=|E|-|V|+1 and H is positive definite on the cycle/gauge quotient. Transient edges give zero rows/columns and cyclic SCCs split into blocks.

theorems.hypotheses: finite W=A/D in non-negative rational scope under uniform scale W(t)=tW
theorems.statement: p(t)=det(DI-tA) is an exact integer polynomial. If support is acyclic, p(t)=D^n and all t>=0 are stable. Otherwise the positive stability endpoint t_c is the smallest positive real root of p. At rational stable t, chi(t)=-t p'(t)/p(t)=tr((I-tW)^(-1)-I) is exact rational. Any positive rational stability potential gives an exact rational lower bound t_c>=1/alpha(h).
theorems.boundary: The critical root itself need not be rational and no floating spectral/root oracle is required for exact rational in-phase certificates.

theorems.hypotheses: finite graph with positive rational edge weights and vertex gauge q'_e=q_e h_t/h_s
theorems.statement: Q_{>0}^x is the direct sum over primes of Z via valuations, so rational gauge classes satisfy H^1(G;Q_{>0}^x) ~= direct_sum_p H^1(G;Z). For a fixed root and underlying spanning tree there is a unique rational gauge with root scale 1 and every tree-edge weight 1; the non-tree rational weights are complete fundamental holonomy coordinates.
theorems.log_readout: ln(q)=sum_p v_p(q) ln p is faithful but derived; the prime-valuation object is an abstract free-abelian module, not generally a discrete Euclidean lattice after log embedding.

theorems.statement: There is a unique decomposition q=s_m(q) t_m(q)^m where s_m is a positive m-power-free integer with prime exponents in {0,...,m-1} and t_m is positive rational. For m=2, s_2 is the squarefree/all-prime C2 parity skeleton and t_2 is the exact even-valuation thickness.
theorems.boundary: Skeleton/parity alone does not determine recurrent stability or loop surplus; thickness remains essential. q/s_m is an exact rational m-th power suitable for the existing BRC ROOT facade.

theorems.hypotheses: finite explicit positive branch variables x_e with W_ij=sum_{e:i->j} x_e
theorems.statement: P_G(x)=det(I-W(x)) is multiaffine. Its nonzero monomials have coefficients +/-1 and are indexed by vertex-disjoint directed cycle systems with sign (-1)^(number of cycles). P_G is identically 1 iff support is acyclic. Each cycle-system monomial is vertex-gauge invariant. On the stable phase Z_loop=1/P_G and Gamma=-ln P_G.
theorems.response_bridge: For explicit edge e, R_e=-q_e P_e/P; diagonal and mixed response identities agree with T19/T20.
theorems.boundary: Alternating determinant signs are inclusion-exclusion bookkeeping, not signed/amplitude BRC branch mass.

theorems.hypotheses: stable finite rational background W with S=(I-W)^(-1); finitely many inserted positive rational events e_r:a_r->b_r of masses delta_r
theorems.statement: Define F_rs=S_{b_r a_s} delta_s. The full updated system is stable iff F is stable. If stable, S_tilde=S+SUD(I-F)^(-1)V^T S, det(I-W_tilde)=det(I-W)det(I-F), Z_loop(W_tilde)=Z_loop(W)Z_loop(F), and Gamma(W_tilde)=Gamma(W)+Gamma(F).
theorems.gauge: Original vertex gauge descends to positive diagonal similarity on event states, so feedback stability/determinant/Gamma are gauge invariant.

theorems.hypotheses: same background as T25; one inserted candidate a->b or one existing explicit branch e:a->b
theorems.statement: For a new edge, kappa=S_ba. If kappa=0 its finite positive insertion radius is infinite; otherwise delta_c=1/kappa and DeltaGamma=-ln(1-delta*kappa) below criticality. For existing branch weight q and response R=qS_ba, the gauge-invariant multiplicative critical factor is Lambda=1+1/R; deleting the branch changes Gamma by ln(1+R).
theorems.polynomial_form: With P=det(I-W) and branch derivative P_e, delta_c=-P/P_e and Lambda=1-P/(q P_e) on recurrent edges.
theorems.thickness_bridge: For q=s_m t^m at fixed mod-m skeleton, thickness scaling t->mu t remains stable exactly while mu^m<Lambda.

theorems.hypotheses: T25 feedback events partitioned into ordered groups A,B and F_A stable
theorems.statement: For one-shot block kernel F=[[F_A,X],[Y,F_B]], the conditional kernel after installing A is F_{B|A}=F_B+Y(I-F_A)^(-1)X. Final stability is equivalent to F_A stable and F_{B|A} stable; det(I-F)=det(I-F_A)det(I-F_{B|A}), so DeltaGamma_{A union B}=DeltaGamma_A+DeltaGamma_{B|A}. Repeated conditioning is associative at the final star/determinant level.
theorems.boundary: Stagewise Gamma attribution depends on order/context although final Gamma is invariant; no unique intrinsic module credit follows.

theorems.hypotheses: finite declared positive feedback-event universe E whose full update is stable; G(A)=Gamma(W_A)-Gamma(W); Z(A)=exp(G(A)) rational
theorems.statement: There are unique nonnegative event-support interactions Phi_T with G(A)=sum_{nonempty T subseteq A} Phi_T. Exact rational factors J_T=exp(Phi_T)=product_{B subseteq T} Z(B)^((-1)^(|T|-|B|)) satisfy J_T>=1 and Z(A)=product_{nonempty T subseteq A} J_T. J_T>1 iff a positive closed event walk has inserted-event support exactly T.
theorems.consequences: G is monotone and supermodular; conditional feedback margins increase and critical radii shrink with positive context. Pair interaction for kernel [[a,b],[c,d]] is ((1-a)(1-d))/((1-a)(1-d)-bc). Pairwise interactions need not be complete: pure higher-order feedback can have all lower-order J=1.
theorems.group_bridge: For disjoint A,B, Z(A union B)/(Z(A)Z(B)) is the product of all J_T crossing the partition and equals the T27 conditional-risk amplification Z(B|A)/Z(B).

theorems.hypotheses: same stable feedback-event scope as T28
theorems.statement: A Möbius-primitive T (J_T>1 and all proper nonempty J_U=1) is a self-return if |T|=1 and otherwise its induced event support is exactly one directed simple cycle. If its rational circuit product is Q_T, then J_T=1/(1-Q_T) and Phi_T=-ln(1-Q_T). The first nonzero interaction order min{|T|:J_T>1} equals directed girth of the feedback-event support.
theorems.number_theory: Q_T is vertex-gauge invariant and carries the T22 prime-valuation and T23 mod-m skeleton/thickness coordinates.
theorems.boundary: Nonprimitive interactions can contain overlapping lower-order circuits and do not reduce to one simple-cycle product.

negative_boundaries.statement: Full rational vertex-gauge cohomology can be nontrivial even when recurrent Gamma/response vanish. A feed-forward diamond can retain a nontrivial rational cross-ratio while having no directed recurrent cycle.
Alternating signs in determinant cycle-system expansion are inclusion-exclusion signs and do not provide signed/amplitude branch-cancellation semantics.
Singleton and pair feedback responses/interactions can all vanish while a pure third- or higher-order event circuit has positive recurrent interaction. Pairwise summaries are not complete in general.
Sequential conditional feedback factors telescope to the intrinsic final Gamma, but stagewise/module attribution generally changes with insertion order. No canonical component credit is implied.

The addendum is finite, positive/non-negative and rational. It does not promote signed/amplitude or complex recurrence, arbitrary exact irrational weights, infinite-state closure, probability/Fisher semantics, or a generic runtime-speedup theorem.

consumption_rule: These theorem IDs are all-research Foundation capabilities but remain lazy. Activate only when the problem actually contains finite rational recurrence, positive rational gauge/holonomy, or declared positive feedback events. Do not force recurrent or feedback semantics onto deterministic/signed problems.
